chapter_name: A GRAIN AS BIG AS A HEN’S EGG

questions.question: Who is the author of the story 'A Grain as big as a Hen’s Egg'?
questions.explanation: The story is written by the famous Russian author Leo Tolstoy.

questions.question: Where did the children find the strange object at the beginning of the story?
questions.explanation: One day some children found the object in a ravine.

questions.question: What was the strange object shaped like?
questions.explanation: The children found a thing shaped like a grain of corn.

questions.question: What size was the object found in the ravine?

options.B: As large as a hen's egg

questions.explanation: The grain of corn was as large as a hen’s egg.

questions.question: What physical feature did the object have down its middle?
questions.explanation: The object had a groove down the middle.

questions.question: How much did the traveller pay the children for the object?
questions.explanation: A traveller passing by bought it from the children for a penny.

questions.question: To whom did the traveller sell the object as a curiosity?
questions.explanation: The traveller took it to town and sold it to the king as a curiosity.

questions.question: What did the King tell his wise men to find out?
questions.explanation: The King called his wise men and told them to find out what the thing was.

questions.question: How did everyone finally realize the object was a grain of corn?

options.A: A wise man cut it open
options.B: A hen pecked at it until she made a hole

questions.explanation: While it was on a window-sill, a hen pecked a hole in it, revealing it was a grain of corn.

questions.question: Were the learned men able to find information about such large corn in their books?

options.B: No, they found nothing about it
options.C: They found it in a geography book
options.D: They found it in a religious text

questions.explanation: The learned men searched their books but could find nothing about it.

questions.question: What did the learned men suggest the King should do to get answers?
questions.explanation: They suggested asking the peasants who may have heard about it from their fathers.

questions.question: How was the first peasant who came to the King described physically?

options.B: Old, bent, ashy pale, and toothless

questions.explanation: The first peasant was old, bent, ashy pale, and toothless.

questions.question: How many crutches did the first old peasant use to walk?
questions.explanation: He managed with the help of two crutches to totter into the King’s presence.

questions.question: What was the King's primary question to the first peasant?

options.B: Where such grain as this grew?

questions.explanation: The King asked if he could tell where such grain as this grew.

questions.question: The first peasant could hardly ________ the grain when shown by the King.
questions.explanation: The King showed him the grain, but the old man could hardly see it.

questions.question: The first peasant was so ________ that he could hardly hear the King.
questions.explanation: The old man was so deaf that he could hardly hear what the King said.

questions.question: What was the first peasant’s final answer regarding the grain?

options.B: He never sowed nor reaped any like it.
options.C: He bought it in the town market.

questions.explanation: He answered that he never sowed or reaped any like it.

questions.question: Who did the first peasant suggest the King should ask?
questions.explanation: He suggested asking his father, who may have heard where such grain grew.

questions.question: How did the second peasant (the father of the first) come to the King?
questions.explanation: The father came walking with one crutch.

questions.question: Was the second peasant able to see the grain better than his son?

options.B: Yes, he was still able to see and took a good look at it.
options.D: He recognized it by smell only.

questions.explanation: The old peasant was still able to see and took a good look at the grain.

questions.question: Regarding buying corn, what did the second peasant say about his time?

options.B: Money was not yet in use.
options.C: They bought corn from foreign countries.

questions.explanation: He said he never bought any because 'in my time money was not yet in use'.

questions.question: According to the second peasant, how did people get corn in his time?

options.B: Every one grew his own corn and shared if needed.
options.C: The King provided it to everyone.

questions.explanation: He noted everyone grew their own and shared with one another when needed.

questions.question: How did the corn in the second peasant's time compare to modern corn?

options.B: It was larger and yielded more flour.
options.D: It was the exact same size.

questions.explanation: He said theirs was 'larger and yielded more flour' than present-day grain.

questions.question: Who did the second peasant suggest the King should ask next?
questions.explanation: He said, 'You had better ask him,' referring to his own father.

questions.question: How did the third peasant (the grandfather of the first) enter the King’s presence?
questions.explanation: He entered walking easily and without crutches.

questions.question: What was the physical condition of the third peasant (the oldest one)?

options.A: His eyes were clear and hearing was good.
options.B: He was ashy pale and toothless.
options.D: He was very sick and needed help.

questions.explanation: His eye was clear, his hearing good, and he spoke distinctly.

questions.question: What did the oldest grandfather do to identify the grain?

options.B: He bit a piece off and tasted it.
options.C: He read a book about it.

questions.explanation: He took the grain, bit a piece off, and tasted it.

questions.question: What was the oldest grandfather’s reaction to the grain?

options.B: He said it’s the very same kind they used to grow.
options.D: He didn't recognize it at all.

questions.explanation: He added, 'It’s the very same kind'.

questions.question: Where did corn like this grow, according to the oldest grandfather?
questions.explanation: He replied that corn like this 'used to grow everywhere in my time'.

questions.question: The oldest grandfather said no one thought of such a 'sin' as what?
questions.explanation: He answered that no one thought of such a sin as buying or selling bread.

questions.question: How did the oldest grandfather describe his 'field'?

options.A: It was a small plot behind his house.
options.B: It was God’s earth; wherever he ploughed was his field.
options.C: He bought it from the King.
options.D: He inherited it from his father.

questions.explanation: He said his field was God’s earth and wherever he ploughed was his field.

questions.question: In the oldest grandfather’s time, what was the only thing men called their own?
questions.explanation: He stated, 'Labour was the only thing men called their own'.

questions.question: What was the King's first 'extra' question to the grandfather?

options.A: How can I grow this corn?
options.B: Why did the earth bear such grain then and has ceased to do so now?

questions.explanation: The King asked why the earth stopped bearing such grain.

questions.question: What was the King's second 'extra' question to the grandfather?

options.A: Why do your grandson and son need crutches while you do not?
options.B: How many sons do you have?
options.C: What is the secret to your clear hearing?
options.D: Can I have some of your seeds?

questions.explanation: The King asked why the younger generations needed crutches while the oldest did not.

questions.question: What reason did the grandfather give for why things had changed?

options.B: Because men have ceased to live by their own labour
options.C: Because the King took all the land
options.D: Because there were too many people

questions.explanation: He said it was because men stopped living by their own labour and started depending on others.

questions.question: The grandfather said they 'coveted not what ________ had produced'.
questions.explanation: The text says they 'coveted not what other had produced'.

questions.question: What does the word 'ravine' mean?
questions.explanation: Glossary: ravine - a very deep narrow valley.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'pondered'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: pondered - thought carefully.

questions.question: The word 'totter' means to ________.
questions.explanation: Glossary: totter - to walk in unsteady way.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'coveted'?

options.B: Strong desire to have something that belongs to others

questions.explanation: Glossary: coveted - strong desire to have something that belongs to others.

questions.question: What does 'ashy pale' describe in the glossary?
questions.explanation: Glossary: ashy pale - unhealthy.

questions.question: Which phrase in the glossary means 'are attracted to / liked to'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: have taken to - are attracted to / liked to.

questions.question: How did the wise men first find out that the curiosity was corn?

options.B: A hen pecked a hole in it.
options.C: They read it in an ancient book.

questions.explanation: A hen flew in and pecked at it until she made a hole.

questions.question: The first peasant needed ________ crutches, the second needed ________, and the third needed ________.
questions.explanation: Text: grandson walks with two, son with one, you [grandfather] with none.

questions.question: What unit of money was the object sold for to the traveller?
questions.explanation: A traveller bought it for a penny.

questions.question: Why were the grains in the grandfather’s time so large?

options.B: People lived according to God’s law and their own labour.
options.C: The King ordered them to be that size.

questions.explanation: The grandfather explained that they lived according to God's law and by their own labour.

questions.question: Which peasant had bright eyes and sound teeth?
questions.explanation: The King noted the oldest peasant had bright eyes, sound teeth, and clear speech.

questions.question: The grandfather said that in his time, 'land was ________'.
questions.explanation: He said, 'Land was free'.

questions.question: What does 'thrash' mean in the glossary?
questions.explanation: Glossary: thrash - to beat repeatedly.

questions.question: What 'sin' did the people of the past avoid, according to the oldest man?
questions.explanation: He stated that 'no one ever thought of such a sin as buying or selling bread'.

questions.question: Where was the object kept when the hen found it?
questions.explanation: The thing was lying on a window-sill when the hen pecked it.

questions.question: How did the grandfather describe his young days regarding corn?

options.B: He lived on corn like this and fed others on it.

questions.explanation: He said he lived on corn like that and fed others on it.

questions.question: What is 'God’s earth' according to the grandfather?
questions.explanation: He said, 'My field was God’s earth'.

questions.question: Which old man had to 'felt it with his hands' because he couldn't see well?
questions.explanation: The first old man could hardly see it, so he felt it with his hands.

questions.question: What did the King call his learned men to do after the hen pecked the hole?

options.B: Find out when and where such corn had grown
options.D: Give more money to the traveller

questions.explanation: He ordered them to find out when and where such corn grew.

questions.question: In the story, 'money was not yet in use' during the time of ________.

options.C: The second peasant and his father

questions.explanation: The second peasant says money was not in use in his time.

questions.question: What was the grandfather’s final comment on why modern life is worse?

options.B: Men have taken to depending on the labour of others.

questions.explanation: He said things are so because men stopped living by their own labor and depend on others.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'distinctly' as used in 'he spoke distinctly'?
questions.explanation: The context implies clear and easy-to-understand speech.

questions.question: How did the second peasant recognize that his own father would know more?

options.A: He was told by the King.
options.B: He heard his father say the grain in his time was even larger.
options.C: He read it in a book.
options.D: He saw it in a dream.

questions.explanation: He said he heard his father say the grain grew larger and yielded more flour in his time.

questions.question: The grandfather's field belonged to whom, according to him?
questions.explanation: He said land was free and a thing no man called his own.

questions.question: What was the 'curiosity' in the story?
questions.explanation: The traveller sold the grain to the King as a curiosity.

questions.question: The first old peasant came to the King ________ into his presence.
questions.explanation: The text says he used crutches to 'totter into the King’s presence'.

questions.question: The King was 'much ________' when the wise men told him it was corn.
questions.explanation: The King was much surprised at this revelation.

questions.question: What does 'yielded' mean in 'yielded more flour'?
questions.explanation: In this context, yield means to produce a crop or product.

questions.question: The oldest peasant bit a piece off the grain and ________ it.
questions.explanation: He bit a piece off and tasted it to identify it.

questions.question: What happened to the first peasant’s teeth?
questions.explanation: The first peasant is described as 'ashy pale and toothless'.

questions.question: The grandfather said: 'Each man had corn ________ of his own'.
questions.explanation: He said they knew nothing of money because each man had enough corn of his own.

questions.question: According to the moral of the story, why do we need crutches today?

options.B: Because we depend on others' labor and not our own.

questions.explanation: The oldest man attributed the physical decline to the loss of self-reliance and labor.

questions.question: What did the oldest man say about 'sin'?

options.B: Buying or selling bread is a sin.
options.C: Eating too much corn is a sin.
options.D: Talking to the King is a sin.

questions.explanation: He said 'no one ever thought of such a sin as buying or selling bread'.

questions.question: The story 'A Grain as big as a Hen’s Egg' suggests that the past was ________ than the present.
questions.explanation: The story highlights the self-reliance, health, and simplicity of the past generations.
